rubrics.criterion: Each remote operation (the local-to-remote transfer, the remote-to-local transfer, and the remote command execution) exposes only capability surface its execution actually consumes; no operation retains members answering another direction's exclusion/compression, or rsync-direction answers when it runs no file transfer.
rubrics.rationale: This is the central obligation of the task: the wide shared contract forced role-foreign capability onto all three operations, so the resolution is only complete when each operation's surface matches its own role.

rubrics.criterion: Where operations still share lifecycle behavior (starting background work and consolidating its outcome), the consuming helpers reach an operation through capability surface no wider than the steps they perform; no driver or consolidation path routes through a contract that also carries transfer-direction or command-synthesis members it never uses.
rubrics.rationale: The prompt asks for dependencies that reflect real use on the consumer side as well; keeping a wide contract behind the remaining shared sequences would relocate, not remove, the problem.

rubrics.criterion: The restructure covers all three operation families in one change, including both pull pacing variants (wait-for-command and poll-alongside), rather than fixing only one operation or one pacing path.
rubrics.rationale: The maintenance concern reported is systemic to the remote-operation flow; a partial restructure leaves the same unused-capability relations alive in the untouched operations and pacing variants.

rubrics.criterion: All construction and call sites of the three operations (and of the helpers that drive them) are updated consistently with the new shape, so the push → execute → pull orchestration builds and runs without legacy bridging code from the previous wide shape.
rubrics.rationale: Splitting contract surface necessarily ripples into every place that constructs an operation or invokes its lifecycle; inconsistent updates would leave duplicate or dead call paths behind.

rubrics.criterion: Direction-specific responsibility ends up with the operation that performs it: exclude-file application per direction, compression levels per direction, pull pacing selection, and remote command-string synthesis each live with (or are invoked by) the code path that actually uses them, instead of being answered uniformly by every operation.
rubrics.rationale: The case was motivated by not being able to see which per-direction answers are consulted at runtime; the repair should make that locally visible rather than spreading it across all operations.

rubrics.criterion: Members that existed only to satisfy the previous wide contract are deleted or are replaced by role-specific equivalents: no unused capability answers, and no category/ marker or helper remains whose only purpose was feeding the old bounds.
rubrics.rationale: The prompt explicitly requires removing scaffolding that exists only to keep the wide shape working; leftover marker categories or blanket capability members would be dead artifacts of the injected design.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not retain no-op or config-plausible stub implementations of capability members merely to keep a prior contract satisfied (for example, keeps operations that answer exclusion/compression questions for a direction or role they never touch).
rubrics.rationale: Keeping the old wide contract compiling with plausible-looking stubs is the most likely shortcut that looks like a repair while preserving exactly the reported unused-capability relations.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not change observable program behavior: console output lines and their ordering, the push → execute → pull sequence, and the exit codes for missing arguments, missing/invalid configuration, and failed push/execute/pull outcomes all remain as before.
rubrics.rationale: This flow is the tool's entire user interface; a restructuring that quietly changes printed lines or failure exit behavior would be a functional regression rather than a refactor.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not alter the remote-transfer mechanics per direction: rsync argument content and order (including remote project-directory creation, ssh usage, compression levels, and which exclude files apply per direction), the ssh command pipe shape for the remote command, and the up-front creation of its result readers are preserved.
rubrics.rationale: These mechanics are the behavior the operations exist to produce; the restructure entertains many valid designs precisely because these outcomes are fixed, and any drift there is a plausible but real regression specific to this case.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not change pull synchronization semantics: a serial pull still waits for the command result before pulling, a parallel pull still pauses, polls alongside the command, and performs the final consistency pull, and perceived pull duration still subtracts the command duration.
rubrics.rationale: The two pull pacing variants are the subtlest timing-sensitive behavior in this repository; a restructure that reroutes crossing-thread completion plumbing can silently change which variant runs when or how durations are measured.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not weaken or delete existing unit tests, nor leave them passing only after edits that reduce what they assert about duration calculation or configuration handling.
rubrics.rationale: The behavioral invariants of this case are guarded by the existing unit tests; rewriting tests to fit a new shape is the shortcut most likely to mask an accidental behavior change.
